A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-Pro research. All 21 pages of v2 and 22 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable. Text, equations, tables, figures, and relocated material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning results across language and image tasks in Section 3, plus X-selection, rank, efficiency, and optimizer-mode experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional training curves, gradient-distance analyses, learning-rate experiments, and Llama-3.1 results.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix C offers efficient and full AdamW modes and explicitly defaults to efficient mode. v3 removes that mode and presents the former full-mode algorithm as its sole AdamW procedure, computing moments of the equivalent full-shaped gradient instead of separate factor gradients. This materially changes the documented optimizer choice; the retained full-mode procedure itself and core gradient-adjustment formulation are unchanged.

E1.justification: The five GLUE tasks, WizardLM/MT-Bench, MetaMathQA/GSM8K, CodeFeedback/HumanEval, and seven image datasets are retained. The added model, learning-rate, and gradient analyses reuse existing data and tasks without establishing a distinct population or input scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds LoRA-GA to the image-classification comparison in Table 3 and the efficiency comparison in Table 4, corresponding to v2 Table 5. LoRA-GA was already evaluated elsewhere in v2, but its participation in these comparisons is new. The GLUE and main LLM comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama-3.1-8B, learning rates 1e-5 and 5e-5, and modulewise gradient-distance measurements at layers 1, 15, and 31. These extend existing evaluations. The reported memory setup changes from one to eight A6000 GPUs, although v3's caption still says one; its timing caption names MetaMathQA while the body retains WizardLM. The exact revised efficiency protocol is therefore ambiguous.

E4.justification: v3 adds convergence comparisons in Figure 3, direct gradient-alignment diagnostics in Appendix D.2, and learning-rate sensitivity in D.3. The existing X-selection ablation moves to D.1 with revised evidence and findings. Conversely, v2's efficient-versus-full AdamW ablation is removed. Together these substantially change the supporting analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs with different random seeds and report means and standard deviations. The added tables continue this practice; v3's explicit three-seed statement for Llama-3.1 does not establish an increased run count or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the rank-8 LoRA-Pro means for MT-Bench/GSM8K/HumanEval from 5.86/54.23/22.76 to 5.72/57.57/22.97 and revises higher-rank results. The X ablation changes from closely grouped scores to a pronounced Sylvester advantage. Efficiency measurements are replaced, optimizer-mode comparison results disappear, and new baseline, diagnostic, learning-rate, and Llama-3.1 results appear. The optimizer and resource-protocol differences prevent treating these revisions as controlled between-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The symmetry-solution expression changes from v2 Equation 16 to v3 Equation 58, removing the outer B and trailing A factors. This is a localized mathematical revision. The equivalent-gradient definition, full-rank assumptions, Theorems 2.1–2.3, and Appendix B proofs otherwise match after equation renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the equivalent-gradient connection, closed-form gradient adjustment, and improved LoRA performance across the same five task families. Additional evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: The X-selection explanation changes from similar performance favoring Sylvester for lower variance to a substantial advantage attributed to subspace selection and faster descent. v3 adds interpretations of gradient alignment and learning-rate robustness, acknowledges unexplained depth-dependent behavior, and states limitations involving low-rank assumptions and incompatibility with DoRA/FLoRA structures. The optimizer-mode memory/stability tradeoff discussion is removed.

D1.justification: v3 removes efficient-mode implementation details while retaining the earlier full-mode pseudocode as Algorithm 2. Hardware and training-time disclosures are revised, with unresolved caption/body inconsistencies in the efficiency experiment. Standard hyperparameter disclosures and the public code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Llama 3, batched low-rank adaptation/FLoRA, and four CLIP or prompt-adaptation works. These modestly extend context and applicability discussion. The principal positioning within PEFT and LoRA research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most of the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and proof narrative is retained. Changes are localized to rewritten experimental interpretations, a shortened Appendix C, the new Appendix D organization, relocation of the X ablation, and added limitations, acknowledgements, and conference-header text.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the analytical displays with three-panel training curves, a 7-by-3 gradient-distance figure, and learning-rate/model comparison tables. It relocates the X-selection table and rank figure, expands comparison tables with LoRA-GA rows, and removes the optimizer-mode table and efficient-mode algorithm display. These changes extend beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 already supplied broad benchmarks and complete proofs. v3 strengthens validation through direct gradient-alignment and convergence evidence, learning-rate and model checks, and LoRA-GA image comparisons, while adding concrete applicability limits. These gains are moderated by removal of the optimizer-mode tradeoff study and inconsistent hardware/timing descriptions in Table 4. Overall, the added validation supports a limited net improvement.
